journey = the act of travelling from one place to another
destination = the place you are travelling to
departure = the moment when a bus, train or plane leaves
arrival = the moment when you reach a place
delay = a situation when something happens later than planned
platform = the area beside the railway tracks where you wait
boarding pass = the ticket you show before you get on a plane
luggage = the bags you take when you travel
suitcase = a large case with a handle for clothes
backpack = a bag you carry on your back
check in = to show your ticket and leave bags at the airport or hotel
take off = when a plane leaves the ground
land = when a plane comes down to the ground
return ticket = a ticket for going and coming back
single ticket = a ticket for going one way only
book a room = to reserve a place to sleep in a hotel
bed and breakfast = a small guest house that includes breakfast
campsite = a place where you can put up a tent
sightseeing = visiting famous places as a tourist
guidebook = a book with maps and tips for tourists
souvenir = a small object you buy to remember a place
package holiday = a holiday where travel and hotel are booked together
go abroad = to travel to another country
get lost = to not know where you are
traffic jam = a long line of cars that cannot move
petrol station = a place where you buy fuel for a car
train timetable = a list of times when trains leave
ferry = a boat that carries people and cars across water
long-distance coach = a comfortable bus for long journeys
aisle = the corridor between seats
window seat = a seat next to the window
cancelled = stopped and not happening as planned
resort = a town or hotel area designed for holidays
landmark = a famous building or place that helps you recognise a city
hitchhike = to travel by asking drivers to take you for free
overland = travelling by road or rail, not by air
airport = the place where planes take off and land
flight = a journey by plane
passenger = a person travelling in a plane, train, bus or car
passport = an official document that lets you travel to another country
visa = a stamp or document that allows you to enter a country
border = the line between two countries
customs = the place at an airport or border where bags are checked
security check = when staff search you and your bags before a flight
passport control = the place where an officer checks your passport
terminal = a large building at an airport for passengers
departure lounge = the waiting area after security, before you board
baggage reclaim = the place where you collect suitcases after a flight
hand luggage = a small bag you take into the cabin
lost luggage = bags that the airline cannot find
runway = the long strip where planes take off and land
direct flight = a flight that does not stop in another city
stopover = a short stay in a city between two flights
cabin crew = the staff who look after passengers on a plane
seat belt = a belt that holds you in your seat
turbulence = sudden movement of a plane caused by air
delayed = happening later than planned
railway station = a building where trains stop for passengers
bus station = a building where coaches and buses start and finish
bus stop = a place at the side of the road where a bus stops
catch a bus = to get on a bus in time
miss the train = to arrive too late to get on a train
change trains = to leave one train and get on another
get on = to enter a bus, train or plane
get off = to leave a bus, train or plane
set off = to start a journey
pick up = to collect a person in a car
drop off = to take a person somewhere in a car and leave them
hire a car = to pay to use a car for a short time
driving licence = the official card that allows you to drive
motorway = a wide road for fast traffic between cities
roundabout = a circular road where several roads meet
traffic lights = red, amber and green lights that control traffic
speed limit = the highest speed that is legal on a road
car park = a place where you leave a car
taxi rank = a place where taxis wait for customers
fare = the money you pay for a bus, train or taxi
travel card = a card that lets you use local buses and trams for a period
season ticket = a ticket you can use many times for a month or year
sleeper = a night train with beds
first class = the more expensive, more comfortable seats
announcement = a spoken message over loudspeakers
waiting room = a room where you sit until a train or bus comes
left luggage = a place at a station where you can leave bags for a few hours
lost property = the office that keeps things people have lost
hotel = a building where you pay to sleep
hostel = cheap shared accommodation, often for young travellers
youth hostel = cheap rooms for young people, often in bunks
guest house = a small house that rents rooms to travellers
reception = the desk in a hotel where you check in
single room = a hotel room for one person
double room = a hotel room with one large bed for two people
twin room = a hotel room with two separate beds
check out = to pay and leave a hotel
fully booked = with no free rooms left
room service = food brought to your hotel room
air conditioning = a system that cools a room
sea view = a window that looks out over the sea
tourist = a person who visits a place for pleasure
tour guide = a person who shows visitors around a place
guided tour = a visit to a place with someone who explains it
excursion = a short trip for pleasure, often in a group
day trip = a journey there and back on the same day
city break = a short holiday in a city, often a weekend
cruise = a holiday on a large ship that visits several ports
harbour = a place on the coast where boats stay safely
coast = the land next to the sea
seaside = a place by the sea where people go on holiday
beach = sand or stones next to the sea
sunbathe = to sit or lie in the sun to get a tan
sunscreen = cream that protects your skin from the sun
tent = a shelter made of cloth that you sleep in outdoors
sleeping bag = a warm bag you sleep in when you camp
hike = a long walk in the countryside or mountains
trail = a path for walkers in the hills or forest
signpost = a sign that shows the way and the distance
map = a drawing of an area that shows roads and places
ask the way = to ask someone how to get to a place
go straight on = to continue in the same direction
turn left = to change direction to the left
turn right = to change direction to the right
travel insurance = money you pay so a company helps if you get ill or lose bags abroad
currency = the money used in a country
exchange rate = how much one currency is worth in another
phrasebook = a small book of useful sentences in another language
brochure = a thin booklet with photos of holidays or places
tourist information = an office that gives maps and advice to visitors
itinerary = a list of places you will visit and when
jet lag = tiredness after a long flight across time zones
abroad = in or to another country
